top_choice_rationale: P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) credits a single, general chemical principle: a small molecule that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target so that cellular ubiquitin-transfer chemistry removes the target catalytically. It has been reproduced independently in many laboratories, is now measured quantitatively (ternary-complex cooperativity, ubiquitination kinetics), and the cereblon strand already explains medicines in patients, so maturity does not hinge on a heterobifunctional approval. The citation covers both strands under one stated mechanism and the three-name allocation follows it. P002 (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a sound, mature, cleanly attributed method with mechanism-led ligand design, so it is my second choice. P003 is chemically real but its lineage exclusions and Chemistry-versus-Medicine fit are unsettled, and P004 rests on in-cell claims that have not yet been measured to a settled standard.
